title: Base change between slice sites realizes localization
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with fibre products [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and let $f:V\to W$ be a morphism in $\mathcal C$. The functor $\beta_f:\mathcal C/W\to\mathcal C/V$, $(T\to W)\mapsto(T\times_WV\to V)$, is continuous for the localized topologies and induces a morphism of sites $\mathcal C/V\to\mathcal C/W$. This morphism has the same geometric morphism of topoi [def-trf-geometric-morphism] as the localization functor $\lambda_f:\mathcal C/V\to\mathcal C/W$, $(T\to V)\mapsto(T\to V\to W)$; in particular, for every sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal C/V$, $(\lambda_{f,*}F)(T\to W)=F(T\times_WV\to V)$, naturally in $T$ and in $F$.

source.place: Tag 09W9, lemma-relocalize-given-fibre-products, clauses (1)-(3) and the proof of the direct-image formula

proof.text: The assignment $\beta_f(T\to W)=(T\times_WV\to V)$ and its action on arrows are functorial by the universal property of fibre products. If $\{T_i\to T\}$ is a covering in $\mathcal C/W$, its underlying family covers in $\mathcal C$ by the localized-topology definition, and $\{T_i\times_WV\to T\times_WV\}$ covers by the site fibre-product axiom. For an arrow $S\to T$ over $W$, the canonical comparison is an isomorphism $\beta_f(S\times_TT_i)=(S\times_TT_i)\times_WV\cong(S\times_WV)\times_{T\times_WV}(T_i\times_WV)$ over $V$, by the universal property of fibre products. This is precisely the second continuity condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Thus $\beta_f$ is continuous.

source.place: Tag 09W9, clause (1), using Definition 00WV and the site fibre-product axiom

proof.text: The site $\mathcal C/W$ is small by the site convention in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. It has terminal object $W/W$ and all pullbacks, computed in $\mathcal C$; hence it has finite limits (binary products are fibre products over $W$, and equalizers are pullbacks of diagonals). Apply [lem-trf-slice-subtopos-site-presentation] to this site and its object $V/W$. The relocalization identification from [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] identifies $((\mathcal C/W)/(V/W))$ with $\mathcal C/V$, and under this identification the localization functor is exactly $\lambda_f:(T\to V)\mapsto(T\to V\to W)$. The cited node gives the adjunction between restriction along $\lambda_f$ and direct image by fibre product with $V/W$; its direct image is precisely precomposition with $\beta_f$. By uniqueness of left adjoints, the sheaf left adjoint associated to the continuous functor $\beta_f$ is this restriction functor, which is left exact by the cited node and preserves colimits as a left adjoint. Thus $\beta_f$ defines a morphism of sites, and its geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] is the localization morphism: their inverse images are the same restriction functor and their direct images are the displayed right adjoint.

source.place: Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products, applied in the localized site $\mathcal C/W$; Tag 09W9, clause (2)

proof.text: For a sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal C/V$, the direct image supplied by the preceding localization calculation evaluates at $T\to W$ as $F(T\times_WV\to V)$. This is the formula in [lem-trf-slice-subtopos-site-presentation] after the substitution $\mathcal C:=\mathcal C/W$ and $U:=V/W$. Restriction maps and morphisms $F\to F'$ are carried componentwise, so the identification is natural in both $T$ and $F$.
